winner.title: Traditional South African Bobotie

evidence.authenticity: Traditional build: soaked bread, curry, fruit chutney, apricot jam, sultanas, bay leaves, turmeric egg custard. Author calls herself a fellow South African and gives her family's version. Origins section is brief (Cape Malay link, every family differs).
evidence.precision: Metric and US units for milk, mince (1 kg) and sultanas. Onions given as 'medium'. 30x20 cm dish. Cues: onions 'soft and translucent', mince 'lost its pinkness', custard 'just set and golden', 10-15 min rest. Only 1 ingredient has a true weight, and spices are in spoons. Oven temperature given in C and F.
evidence.testing: Rating 4.99 from 181 ratings. Troubleshooting covers scrambled custard (cool the mince 5-10 min first), dry bobotie (use medium-fat mince, keep the bread) and too sweet. Explains that the egg stirred into the mince gives a sliceable texture. Home-cook testing, not a test kitchen.
evidence.photos: Per WebFetch, most steps have a photo, from soaking the bread through pouring the custard and placing the bay leaves. Schema has no step images.
evidence.efficiency: Bread soaks while the mince cooks. Single pan plus one dish. About 1h20 total, realistic. One extra step: the egg stirred into the mince.
evidence.access: Mrs Ball's chutney is the classic choice, but mango or peach chutney works. Apricot jam and Worcestershire sauce are in any US grocery. No hard-to-find items.

winner.why: It has the most traditional method, a large base of positive reviews (181 at 4.99), real troubleshooting and step photos, which the runner-up and the weighted-metric Pants Down recipe lack in combination.

runnerUp.title: Bobotie

evidence.authenticity: Recipe from Gramadoelas, a well-known Johannesburg restaurant. Classic lamb, curry, bread, apple, raisins, almonds, bay leaves, milk and egg topping.
evidence.precision: Cups and spoons only. '1 Granny Smith apple', no dish size. Cues such as 'soft and translucent' and 'browned and firm' are present, and the oven is at 350 F.
evidence.testing: 99 ratings at 5.0 and NYT editorial process.
evidence.photos: Not visible through read. NYT content may be hidden behind the login, so this was not marked down heavily.
evidence.efficiency: Concise 1-hour recipe. The bread-squeeze step is standard.
evidence.access: Everything is at a US grocery.

runnerUp.why: Authentic and well rated, but it has fewer doneness cues and no dish size, and its photos can't be confirmed.

searches: traditional South African bobotie recipe Cape Malay
notes: Searches were English only. The dish name is the same in South Africa, so no separate native-language search was run. Most English versions agree on the core: curried mince, bread soaked in milk, fruit and chutney, bay leaves and a custard top. Pants Down (66) has weights for 20 ingredients and a yellow rice recipe, but its step order is muddled and its photos could not be confirmed. If a yellow rice companion is wanted, that page covers it. The NYT Komolafe version uses garam masala and a larger egg custard, so it is a looser variant.
